name: CampaignFlow 30-Minute Planning Framework
source: CampaignFlow_30_Minute_Planning_Framework_v2 (Omni OS). Internal planning synthesis, not medical, legal, regulatory or promotional approval.
principle: Six steps from the brand plan to build-ready activation. Each step answers one question, consumes the APPROVED output before it, and hands a concrete artefact to the next. If a step cannot be filled, go back to the owner of the missing decision. Gaps become questions, never inventions.
from_brand_plan: Eligible brand audience (specialties and roles: primary prescriber vs adjacent pathway)
not_from_brand_plan: Segment sizes against the live target list
Digital affinity, movability and final channel mix
vocabulary: The journey is one part of the engagement plan.
Keeps it separate from the brand objective.
What the field and CRM teams call it.
Existing: lifecycle stages. Launch: Primary / Secondary / Tertiary.
What the brand wants for a lifecycle state (Activate / Grow / Retain / Support / Reactivate / Enable).
How much to invest: High / Standard / Low, from step 02.
Scored in step 03 to weight digital-led vs field-led mix.
Scored in step 04; adjusts journey intensity and cadence only.
Exit is meaningful only, not silence.
Where the HCP goes after a valid exit.
The build-ready Campaign Operations handoff; references rule IDs.

steps.name: Campaign objective card
steps.question: What must this campaign achieve, for whom, and under which brand strategy and guardrails?
steps.reads: The brand plan: therapy area, market, brand objective, target audience, strategic imperatives, KPIs and targets, medical and compliance guardrails.
decides: Audience prioritization: who to influence, from brand eligibility and therapy-area opportunity
Behavioural ambition: what change to drive
Strategic imperative: why the campaign matters
Success alignment: inherit the brand plan's KPIs
steps.produces: One seven-field card: campaign objective, target audience (primary prescriber and adjacent pathway), current behaviour, desired behaviour, strategic imperative, messaging & guardrails, channel priorities. Everything quoted or synthesized from the brand plan; anything missing raised as a question.
rules: Use the brand's own words, not generic phrasing.
Activate / Grow / Retain / Support / Reactivate are strategic priorities, not segment names.
Capture primary prescribers AND adjacent pathway roles; step 02 builds separate universes from this field.
Channel priorities here are high-level brand priorities only; the final mix is decided in step 03.
Campaign start dates are set in the engagement plan, not the brand plan: allow MLR clearance (e.g. 45 days) after approval.

steps.name: Target audience segmentation
steps.question: Who is in scope, how are they segmented, and who gets greater campaign focus?
steps.reads: The approved objective card; HCP and market data (existing brands) or IQVIA (launch brands); consent and eligibility.

decisions: Target universe: eligible HCPs; primary prescriber universe vs separate adjacent pathway universe (an HCP in both is primary)
Lifecycle segmentation by prescribing + engagement: Awareness, Trialist, Adopter, Advocate, Stopper (one HCP, one segment)
Strategic priority mapped from the brand plan to the lifecycle segment
Prioritization: brand opportunity x HCP reachability -> matrix position -> investment priority (High / Standard / Low) and desired progression

lifecycle.definition: No brand prescriptions yet; eligible HCP with potential to adopt.
Early brand experience; initial Rx or sample, no sustained adoption.
Consistent brand prescribing; sustained Rx behaviour.
Sustained adoption with demonstrated engagement and advocacy.

existing.adjacent: Adjacent pathway roles are a separate universe with strategic priority Enable, scored on pathway influence signals (referrals, tests, protocols), with pathway KPIs, not brand Rx.

scoring.brand_opportunity: High: high prescribing potential and adoption opportunity. Medium: moderate. Low: limited potential or established adoption. Signals: Rx potential, brand share, adoption opportunity, patient opportunity.
scoring.hcp_reachability: High: multiple viable routes. Medium: one viable route. Low: limited reachable routes. Signals: consent, rep access, digital access, engagement history.

decisions: Eligibility gates (IQVIA): specialty, therapy-area relevance, geography, relevant category/class prescribing. Fail any gate -> out of universe.
Opportunity segmentation: Primary (01, initial launch investment), Secondary (02, subsequent expansion), Tertiary (03, broader coverage, lighter intensity). Segment = launch priority.
launch.rule: IQVIA only. Do not infer engagement history, digital affinity, reachability, lifecycle stage or journey state. Journey design waits for engagement or brand-response data.

rules: Eligibility, consent, identity and compliance are gates before scoring: no consent -> suppress / consent acquisition; no reachable consented channel -> hold / suppress.
Only brand opportunity and HCP reachability determine the matrix position; the matrix does not create strategic priority.
Scoring cut-offs are business-owned and market-specific: do not invent thresholds.
Digital affinity is scored in step 03; movability in step 04.
steps.produces: Existing: lifecycle segment, strategic priority, matrix position, investment priority, desired progression (plus adjacent universe with Enable). Launch: eligibility status, launch segment, launch priority, supporting IQVIA attributes.

steps.name: Channel planning
steps.question: For this audience and desired progression, which channels deliver the approved message?
steps.reads: Segmented target list (lifecycle, strategic priority, desired progression, investment priority), approved message modules, brand channel priorities (candidates, not the final mix).
checks: 01 Message fit: can the channel deliver the approved message for this movement? Remove channels with no relevant message role.
02 HCP engagement: how does this HCP engage across channels? Weight the mix to observed engagement.
03 Consent & access: can we legally and operationally reach this HCP on this channel? Remove channels blocked by consent, market rules or missing access.
04 Execution feasibility: can it be activated within operational constraints? Remove or adjust on capacity and coordination.

investment_intensity.Standard: Digital-first; field on signal or high value.

steps.digital_affinity: High: digital-led mix (email, webinar, portal lead). Medium: balanced digital and field. Low: field- or event-weighted for the same strategic priority.
channel_jobs: Depth, conversion destination (CTA destination, not counted in live mix)
rules: Progression defines the engagement need; channel planning decides how to deliver it.
Hard constraints are gates; they cannot be offset by opportunity or reachability. No approved module -> no channel.
Live mix: 2 channels by default, 3 maximum per audience x progression.
Email HOE and Email VAE are separate channels (different consent, owners, costs, roles). Never write just 'email'.
steps.produces: Channel plan: selected channels x message modules per audience x progression (2 default, 3 max); execution constraints (frequency, coordination, suppression); gap register (missing consent, content or channel access).

steps.name: Journey design
steps.question: How do we engage: signal -> next-best tactic -> wait / hold -> next interaction -> progression?
steps.reads: Channel plan and execution constraints from step 03; segmented target list (desired progression, priorities); approved content modules and CTAs; consent records; engagement history.

journey_types.orchestrates: First education sequence (e.g. MOA -> Efficacy -> Dosing), 7-day waits; no signal -> hold 14 days, alternate content/channel, rep follow-up
Timed core sequence with survey and content checks; a qualifying survey opens a two-step invitation and automated follow-up without stopping the core
journey_types.next: Story Follow-up, or remain in Nurture

journey_types.orchestrates: Automated follow-up, open/complete checks, one reminder after 7 days, then human review and pursue / close
Lead email, 7-day no-open retry, 21-day no-open field suggestion, rep-triggered email and landing page writing to the CDP; awareness assigned only on an approved evidence rule

plays: Follow-up after a high-intent signal (click, download, site depth)
Alternate route after a wait with no signal; HCP stays in the journey
Opt out, fatigue hold, journey complete, next-journey handoff
branches: Access CTA click + access-tool site action
Move to access-support / Education path; suppress generic module only
Five touchpoints / 180 days with no interaction
Lower-intensity re-engagement / evergreen path; still in the universe
Rep visit logged or congress scan during a digital journey
Pause or branch per field coordination; store entry source
Exit current journey; enter Retention, Advocacy or Reactivation
steps.movability: High: standard cadence, full progression path. Medium: moderated cadence or narrower tactic set. Low (structural barrier): lighter touch or access-support module. Strategic priority unchanged.
rules: Non-engagement is not exit: no open / no click -> wait, retry or another approved channel.
Exit is meaningful only: sequence complete, next-journey handoff, opt-out, policy inactivity. Completing one journey exits that journey only.
Opt-out (by the HCP, a consent action) and exit criteria (set by us) are separate fields.
Step 04 sequences the approved channel plan; it does not re-select channels.
Wait periods are configurable; example timings are templates (mark them CONFIGURABLE).
Field coordination: e.g. pause overlapping email 72 hours around a logged rep visit.
Non-engager policy: 180-day look-back; five touchpoints with no interaction -> lower intensity; a second quiet cycle -> deliberate policy exit.
Build Welcome first; add other journeys only when their survey, content, identity, consent and field signals are trusted.
steps.produces: Customer engagement plan: journey catalog (entry, orchestration, exit, next journey), tactic catalog (segment, channel, content, CTA, wait/hold, signal, fatigue, next tactic), journey sequences, branch catalog, journey-rule requirements for step 05, measurement (progression, CTA completion, handoffs, not opens alone), gap register.

steps.name: Omnichannel planning
steps.owner: Brand Manager + Campaign Orchestrator / Omnichannel lead
steps.question: What IF/THEN rules govern signal -> tactic -> wait -> next interaction across the approved channels?
steps.reads: Approved customer engagement plan; channel plan and content modules; segmented list and progression; consent, contact, Medical and PV policies; CRM / CDP / SFMC capability constraints.
decides: Meaningful engagement, weak evidence, bot/fake open, no-response, access need, progression
Tactic = intended action; touchpoint = what the HCP experiences
Which channel starts, follows a signal, covers no response
Which signal advances, holds, changes module, triggers field, moves journey
Wait, retry, reduce intensity, other approved channel; silence alone does not exit
Which qualified evidence changes state or hands off
Consent, cap, quiet-hour, field/event, content-expiry, portfolio controls
When no action is eligible or confidence is insufficient
rules: Business rules, not platform build: no SFMC / CRM / CDP configuration, QA records, budget/KPI baselines or MLR approval.
Rules before ranking: eligibility, consent, caps, content status, market/indication, suppression and MI/PV routing are hard gates, never traded for predicted engagement.
Single rule source: stable rule IDs here; step 06 references them.
Blocking gaps return upstream to steps 01-04.
steps.approvals: Brand Manager + Omnichannel / Campaign Orchestrator approve business fidelity; Journey Design Authority and policy owners approve rule boundaries.
steps.produces: Omnichannel Plan / Orchestration Specification: event dictionary, per-channel business-rule catalog with rule IDs, approved journey/action/content/channel links, policy controls and safe outcomes.

steps.name: Campaign brief
steps.owner: Campaign Orchestrator / Campaign Operations with Data and Compliance
steps.question: What must Campaign Operations configure, test, approve and release so the planned journeys work exactly as intended?
steps.reads: Approved Omnichannel Plan; frozen step 01-04 sources; audience/data source and event availability; content approval, consent and policy metadata; platform constraints.
actions: Package rules by ID (journey, tactic, content)
sections: Campaign objective, target audience, strategic priority, desired progression, scope and valid window
Target list/version, inclusion/exclusion, lifecycle or launch segment, consent purpose, suppression sources
Approved journey, tactic and rule IDs plus platform fields to implement them
Approved asset/module/version and channel IDs, language, market, expiry, delivery mapping
Read-only step 05 rule IDs for IF/THEN, caps, collision, fatigue, suppression, MI/PV, safe fallback
Source fields, event definitions, identity matching, timestamps, quality flags, refresh/latency
Decision exposure, progression, CTA/outcome, guardrails, experiment/control, reporting windows
Test scenarios, expected results, approvers, defects, go/no-go, activation, rollback
qa_scenarios: Block or select an approved fallback
Wait / lower intensity / alternate channel; HCP remains in target audience
Rep visit collides with digital tactic
Pause or reschedule under field-coordination policy
Promotional path pauses; route to Medical Information
No duplicate action; preserve event-time ordering
definition_of_done: Business-ready: audience, purpose, content, channels, journey logic, measures and owners in business language
Build-ready: every trigger, wait, branch, suppression, exit, data field and expected result explicit enough to configure and test
Decision-ready: if agentic NBA is used, the permitted action/content/channel space and NO_ACTION behaviour are machine-readable and versioned
Release-ready: QA/UAT passes, approvals attached, monitoring active, rollback prepared
rules: Package, do not re-decide: a missing business rule returns to step 05.
Hard gates remove an action; they are never soft score penalties.
Explicit preference wins over predicted digital affinity.
Final recheck of consent, suppression, cap and asset expiry immediately before execution.
steps.produces: Campaign Brief: the nine sections, rule-ID build mapping per journey, QA/UAT scenarios with expected results, approvals and release/rollback, definition of done.

open_items: Segment counts against a live target list
Needs a real target list and data refresh
Modules may not exist or may be in MLR
Look-back windows (180 days engagement, 4 weeks prescribing)
